text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
EarnsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHall(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of time eating and catching up with friends in campus dining halls.
MarysSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → EarnsMoney(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHall(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People either order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of time eating and catching up in campus dining halls.
Hannah(MarysSchool) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
∀x ((WorksInStudentJobs(x) ∧ Hannah(x) ∧ EarnsMoney(x)) → (¬PickyEater(x) ∧ EarnsMoney(x))) ::: If Hannah works in student jobs and needs to earn money, then she is not picky and needs to earn money.

Conclusion:
Hannah(MarysSchool) ∧ ¬PickyEater(MarysSchool) ∧ SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(MarysSchool) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school, she is not a picky eater, and spends a lot of her time eating and catching up in campus dining halls.
